title: Optimal conversion from Rényi Differential Privacy to $f$-Differential Privacy
claim: The feasible privacy region has a tight lower boundary, touched at every point by some simple binary mechanism, so it cannot be improved.
layout: 1 panel, square axes, curves converge on a boundary, legend top-right
description: A single square plot of Type I error (alpha, x-axis) against Type II error (beta, y-axis), both from 0 to 1. A light-blue shaded area marks the RDP privacy region. Its lower edge is a bold blue convex curve running from the top-left to the bottom-right, and a dotted diagonal marks random guessing. Several thin piecewise-linear trade-off curves for randomized response mechanisms cross the region. The symmetric mechanism is red, and the asymmetric ones run from purple through teal to green. Each line touches the bold boundary at one marked dot, which shows the boundary is tight. A large legend in the upper right lists the curve parameters. The eye goes first to the bold blue curve and the colored dots on it.
caption: Visualization of the $\tau$-order RDP privacy region $R_{D_\tau}(\rho)$ for $\tau=1.5$ and $\rho=0.75$. The bold blue line depicts the lower boundary $f_{\tau, \rho}(\alpha)$, and the shaded region corresponds to $R_{D_\tau}(\rho)$. The piecewise linear trade-off functions correspond to specific Randomized Response mechanisms satisfying the $(1.5, 0.75)$-RDP constraint: the red line denotes the symmetric RR mechanism ($p=0.75$) and the remaining lines denote the asymmetric RR mechanisms with varying parameters $p$ and $q$. For every point on the lower boundary, there exists a Randomized Response mechanism whose trade-off function touches the boundary at exactly that point, establishing that the boundary cannot be tightened without excluding valid mechanisms (Proposition [ref]).
abstract: We prove the conjecture stated in Appendix F.3 of \citet{zhu2022optimalaccountingdifferentialprivacy}: among all conversion rules that map a RÃ©nyi Differential Privacy (RDP) profile $Ï\mapsto Ï(Ï)$ to a valid hypothesis-testing trade-off $f$, the rule based on the intersection of single-order RDP privacy regions is optimal. This optimality holds simultaneously for all valid RDP profiles and for all Type I error levels $Î±$. Concretely, we show that in the space of trade-off functions, the tightest possible bound is $f_{Ï(\cdot)}(Î±) = \sup_{Ï\geq 0.5} f_{Ï,Ï(Ï)}(Î±)$: the pointwise maximum of the single-order bounds for each RDP privacy region. Our proof unifies and sharpens the insights of \citet{balle2019hypothesistestinginterpretationsrenyi}, \citet{asoodeh2021variantsdifferentialprivacylossless}, and \citet{zhu2022optimalaccountingdifferentialprivacy}. Our analysis relies on a precise geometric characterization of the RDP privacy region, leveraging its convexity and the fact that its boundary is determined exclusively by Bernoulli mechanisms. Our results establish that the \enquote{intersection-of-RDP-privacy-regions} rule is not only valid, but optimal: no other black-box conversion can uniformly dominate it in the Blackwell sense, marking the fundamental limit of what can be inferred about a mechanism's privacy solely from its RDP guarantees.
